story.headline: Measured against the same point in 2024, every comparable measure is more Democratic. Measured against 2022, it isn't, because Democrats have moved from mail ballots to voting early in person.

story.compare_note: Democratic share of mail-ballot requests (CNN/Catalist, Oct 1). Gray dot is the same point in 2024. Virginia's early voters with only Democratic primary history lead those with only GOP history by 18 points, vs. 8 in 2024; Ohio's early electorate is about 27 points more Democratic than at this point in 2024 (CNN, Oct 8). CNN also found that the 2022 request pools were more Democratic than 2026's in every listed state except Iowa.

bullets.title: The edge over 2024 is real but partly a change in how Democrats vote.
bullets.html: Democratic mail requests in North Carolina are down 40% from 2022, against 18% for Republicans, yet Democrats are returning ballots faster (22% returned vs. 17% in 2022). In an NBC poll, 23% of Democrats plan to vote by mail, down from 34% in 2024, and 36% plan to vote early in person, up from 30%. Democrats' confidence that the Postal Service will deliver ballots on time fell from 86% to 60% (Marist).

bullets.title: Volume against 2022 is mixed.
bullets.html: Michigan's returned absentee ballots are up 30% from the same point in 2022 (201,909 vs. 155,142) and Minnesota's up 29% (127,682 vs. 99,252). North Carolina is 22.5% behind (27,854 vs. 35,958).

bullets.title: Virginia is more Democratic but slower.
bullets.html: State Navigate estimates its early vote is 4.2 points more Democratic than 2025's (6.5 in VA-1, 8.6 in VA-9). Turnout runs 23% behind the same point in 2024, per TargetSmart.

bullets.title: The early electorate is old.
bullets.html: Voters 65 and older cast about two-thirds of returned ballots in Michigan, Pennsylvania and Georgia; 18–25s cast 2–6%. It will get younger as in-person voting opens.

bullets.title: Democratic data firms report a Latino and Black surge.
bullets.html: TargetSmart's Tom Bonier says the Hispanic share of the early vote is above the same point in 2022 in more than 94% of 229 comparable counties, with about 112,000 Latino early votes vs. 106,000 at this point in 2024. No independent replication yet.

bullets.title: Republicans say they vote later.
bullets.html: National Review's Noah Rothman argues Democrats will lead the early vote, "but perhaps not by the margins the party expects," because their own warnings eroded trust in mail. A Virginia GOP volunteer told the Daily Signal that "Republicans show up on Election Day more so." No quantitative RNC early-vote claims for 2026 turned up.

bullets.title: Nevada is the cautionary tale.
bullets.html: Its first 2,851 ballots were 48% Democratic and 22% Republican; Jon Ralston called that meaningless this early. In 2024 Democrats led Nevada's mail vote, Republicans led the total early vote, and Trump won.

story.calendar_note: Iowa and Kansas mail ballots go out Oct 14. Pennsylvania and New Hampshire have no early in-person voting.
story.cast_at_note: Ballots counted (UF Election Lab, 34 states + DC, state data as of Oct 5-12) when these comparisons were compiled; sets the automatic early-vote weight.
story.signals_verdict: Against 2024 the early vote looks more Democratic; against 2022 it looks less so. Both comparisons are bent by Democrats switching from mail to in-person voting, so the fair read is that the early vote is consistent with the polls. The first clean test is in-person voting in Georgia (from Oct 13) and North Carolina (from Oct 15).

signals.title: Ohio's early electorate is far more Democratic than in 2024
signals.value: About 27 points more Democratic than at this point in 2024, by primary history. Counties Trump won by 20+ are R+5, vs. R+30 then.
signals.catch: 2024 was a presidential year, and Ohio Republicans are shifting from mail to in person: mail is at 25% of its 2024 pace, in-person at 72%.
signals.src: CNN, using Ohio Secretary of State data, Oct 11

signals.title: Virginia's early voters lean further Democratic than in 2024
signals.value: Voters with only Democratic primary history lead those with only GOP history by 18 points, vs. 8 at this point in 2024. In VA-1: D+15, vs. about R+3.
signals.catch: Primary history isn't a vote, and 2024 had a presidential-year electorate.

signals.title: Democrats are returning their ballots faster than in 2022
signals.value: North Carolina: 22% of Democrats' requested ballots are back, vs. 17% at this point in 2022. Pennsylvania: 20% vs. 15%.
signals.catch: It could be enthusiasm, or worry that the mail will be slow; NBC/Penn say the data can't tell yet.

signals.title: Democrats' share of mail requests is up from 2024
signals.value: Iowa 67% vs. 54% at the same point in 2024; North Carolina 42% vs. 36%; Pennsylvania 66% vs. 62%; Maine 57% vs. 53%.
signals.catch: Against 2022 the same shares are lower everywhere except Iowa (see the other column).

signals.title: Trump country in New Jersey is voting less Republican
signals.value: In counties Trump won by 20+, the pre-election vote has shifted nearly 11 points toward Democrats vs. this point in 2024.
signals.catch: Small counties and a presidential-year baseline.

signals.title: Michigan's mail returns are up 30% on 2022
signals.value: 201,909 ballots returned by Oct 6, vs. 155,142 at the same point in 2022; requests are up 27%.
signals.catch: Michigan has no party registration, so this measures turnout, not direction. Most requests come from the permanent mail list.

signals.title: Against 2022, Democrats' share of mail requests is down
signals.value: Lower now than at this point in 2022 in every state CNN checked except Iowa.
signals.catch: Democrats are moving from mail to early in-person voting: 23% plan to vote by mail, down from 34% in 2024 (NBC poll).

signals.title: North Carolina Democrats requested far fewer mail ballots
signals.value: Requests vs. the same point in 2022: Democrats down 42%, Republicans down 19%.
signals.catch: Same mode shift. North Carolina's in-person early voting, where most of its vote is cast, starts Oct 15.

signals.title: Pennsylvania Republicans are requesting more mail ballots
signals.value: Requests vs. the same point in 2022: Republicans up 18%, Democrats down 14%.
signals.catch: Republicans have been urged to vote by mail this year, so more requests may be a change of method rather than more voters.

signals.title: Georgia's mail requests fell more in Democratic areas
signals.value: Down 52% in heavily Harris precincts vs. 39% in heavily Trump precincts.
signals.catch: Mail is a small slice of Georgia's vote; in-person early voting starts Oct 13.

signals.title: An older early electorate
signals.value: Voters 65+ are a bigger share of mail requests than at this point in 2022 or 2024 in nearly every state.
signals.catch: Polls have seniors about even this year, so older doesn't mean Republican the way it used to; fewer young voters is the real cost to Democrats.
